title: Logical-Space Theory of Ordered-Statistics Decoding for Quantum LDPC Codes
abstract: Quantum decoding succeeds when a correction matches the logical class of the error, whereas ordered-statistics decoding (OSD) searches a finite list of physical corrections. We connect these spaces through a rank-$k$ logical-signature map $M_{\rm log}:\mathbb F_2^q\to\mathbb F_2^k$. For fixed, error-independent orderings it yields the exact logical-signature distribution, the OSD-0 logical error rate, and the logical-class coverage of any fixed list. For minimum-cost list decoding we prove $P_L=P_{\rm miss}+P_{\rm sel}$, separating absent-class from wrong-selection failures. Hypergraph-product and bivariate-bicycle codes are consistent with the coverage predictions. On the $[\![144,12,12]\!]$ gross code, 672 coverage-aware candidates outperform 899 combination-sweep candidates (paired McNemar $p=0.013$), while two lists with identical logical coverage give $P_L=11.30\%$ and $3.78\%$; the signature-based coverage compression persists across 30 random column orderings. Logical coverage and within-class representative selection are therefore complementary resources that candidate count alone does not capture. The framework guides OSD list construction and compression by identifying coverage requirements and distinguishing coverage losses from failures of representative selection.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework to analyze the performance of quantum LDPC code decoders by mapping physical errors to a logical signature space. It rigorously proves that the overall logical error rate decomposes into two distinct failure types: missing the true logical class (coverage miss) or selecting the wrong representative within the correct class (selection failure). This decomposition guides the construction of more efficient, coverage-aware decoding lists.
main_problem: The paper addresses how to determine the logical error rate for quantum Low-Density Parity-Check (LDPC) codes when using candidate-based decoding methods like Ordered-Statistics Decoding (OSD).
main_result: The logical error rate ($P_L$) is rigorously decomposed into two complementary failure modes: coverage miss ($P_{	ext{miss}}$) and wrong selection ($P_{	ext{sel}}$).
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework using a logical-signature map ($M_{	ext{log}}$) to algebraically connect physical error spaces to the logical space, allowing for exact calculation of error probabilities.
model_or_system: The study focuses on quantum LDPC codes, specifically analyzing decoding performance for CSS quantum codes under X-error decoding assumptions.
key_observables: Logical Error Rate ($P_L$), Coverage Probability ($P_{	ext{cover}}$), $P_{	ext{miss}}$, and $P_{	ext{sel}}$.
important_parameters: The noise probability ($p$) of the i.i.d. bit-flip channel, and the structure of the code (e.g., the $[\![144,12,12]\!]$ gross code).
main_assumptions: The exact distributional results are derived under the assumption of fixed, error-independent column orderings and an i.i.d. bit-flip channel.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the logical-space structure, mapping free variables to logical displacements, and showing $P_{	ext{miss}}(p)$ curves comparing theoretical results with Monte Carlo simulations.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the logical-signature map and the OSD-0 rate, then proves the exact decomposition $P_L = P_{	ext{miss}} + P_{	ext{sel}}$, and finally applies this framework to compare various decoding strategies on specific quantum codes.
why_interesting: While focused on quantum error correction, the rigorous mathematical decomposition of failure mechanisms ($P_{	ext{miss}}$ vs $P_{	ext{sel}}$) provides a generalizable theoretical tool for analyzing the limitations of any finite-list decoding scheme in quantum information.
